data.clinical_result_summary: HRS-8080 demonstrated a favorable safety and tolerability profile and encouraging antitumor activity in ESR1-mutant ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer. These findings support ongoing clinical development both as monotherapy and in combination regimens.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with locally advanced/metastatic ER+/HER2- breast cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: HRS-8080, an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD), in ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer (aBC) with ESR1 mutations (ESR1m): Results from a first-in-human phase 1 trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: The Phase I/II studies provided clinical evidence of a favorable benefit-risk profile for EN002-gel as a novel topical therapy in patients with Bowen's disease, basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or actinic keratosis. Phase II drug treatment for actinic keratosis is expected to be completed in May 2026, and new results will be presented at the meeting.
clinical_result_indication_detail: adult patients with actinic keratosis or non-melanoma skin cancer including basal cell carcinoma, Bowen's disease, and low-risk squamous cell carcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-in-human phase I/II study of EN002-gel, a first-in-class drip inhibitor, in non-melanoma skin cancer and actinic keratosis.

data.clinical_result_summary: Survivin-specific immune responses were strongly enriched among patients with clinical benefit, supporting survivin as an active target in ovarian cancer. HLA typing demonstrated broad coverage of Maveropepimut-S epitopes across patients, and molecular subtype may have influenced immune responses. These findings support biomarker-integrated studies to optimize immunotherapy combinations in ovarian cancer.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with metastatic ovarian cancer, including platinum-sensitive high-grade serous ovarian cancer, platinum-resistant high-grade serous ovarian cancer, and rare ovarian cancer histologies.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Vaccine-induced immune responses, HLA genotyping, and molecular profiling in patients with metastatic ovarian cancer (the PESCO trial).

data.clinical_result_summary: Camrelizumab combined with capecitabine as maintenance therapy appeared to prolong survival in patients with metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and showed favorable efficacy and safety. Further validation is needed as enrollment is ongoing.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Camrelizumab combined with capecitabine as maintenance therapy for metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: A phase II single-arm clinical trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: In Chinese patients with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered HR+/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy ± CDK4/6 inhibitors, capivasertib plus fulvestrant showed encouraging preliminary efficacy and safety. Follow-up is ongoing.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Chinese patients with HR+/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Capivasertib plus fulvestrant in Chinese patients with HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer: Interim analysis of CAPItrue.

data.clinical_result_summary: Staged combination therapy with encorafenib, binimetinib, and cetuximab showed potential to achieve disease control in patients with BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer who were refractory to encorafenib plus cetuximab. The primary 12-week progression-free survival rate endpoint was met, and no new safety signal was identified.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer who were refractory to encorafenib plus cetuximab
data.clinical_result_paper_title: BAYONET trial: A multicenter phase II trial of staged combination with encorafenib + binimetinib + cetuximab following encorafenib + cetuximab in patients with BRAFV600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: This analysis showed survival and response benefits of ciltacabtagene autoleucel in patients with high- and standard-risk cytogenetics who achieved a partial response or better to bridging therapy, with more than 85% of patients alive at 30 months. No patients had immune effector cell-parkinsonism, and infections were a key cause of nonrelapse mortality. These data highlight the profound benefit that ciltacabtagene autoleucel can provide when multiple myeloma is well controlled at the time of infusion.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The analysis included patients with lenalidomide-refractory multiple myeloma after 1–3 lines of therapy who received ciltacabtagene autoleucel as study treatment and achieved a partial response or better to bridging therapy, analyzed according to high-risk cytogenetics, defined by positivity for del(17)p, t(14;16), t(4;14), or gain/amp(1q), or standard-risk cytogenetics, defined by negativity for these mutations.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel in lenalidomide-refractory multiple myeloma responding to bridging therapy: CARTITUDE-4 cytogenetic subgroup analysis.

data.clinical_result_summary: Palliative neck RT combined with lenvatinib/pembrolizumab for BRAF wild-type anaplastic thyroid cancer appears safe and may improve surgical resectability in patients with initially unresectable disease or high baseline surgical morbidity. Patients who proceeded to neck surgery had a high pathologic complete response rate and significantly prolonged OS and PFS with a low rate of locoregional relapse.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with BRAF wild-type anaplastic thyroid cancer treated with palliative neck radiotherapy (≤45 Gy) administered five days before to 21 days after first-line lenvatinib/pembrolizumab, including those with initially unresectable disease or high baseline surgical morbidity.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Palliative neck radiation therapy (RT) in combination with lenvatinib/pembrolizumab (L/P) in BRAF wild-type anaplastic thyroid cancer (BRAF-WT ATC).

data.clinical_result_summary: Adebrelimab combined with lenvatinib showed encouraging activity in second-line advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, with a median overall survival of 12.2 months. The benefit appeared to persist in a high-risk population with substantial tumor burden and predominantly Child-Pugh class B liver function, supporting further randomized validation.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with unresectable or metastatic intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who had experienced progression or intolerance to first-line chemotherapy
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Phase II clinical study of the efficacy and safety of adebrelimab in combination with lenvatinib as second-line treatment for advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: Updated results.

data.clinical_result_summary: SL105, an autologous dual-epitope nanobody CD5 CAR-T therapy, demonstrated a favorable safety profile and encouraging efficacy in patients with relapsed or refractory T-ALL/PTCL. The recommended phase 2 dose was established, supporting further evaluation in an ongoing phase 2 study.
clinical_result_indication_name: T细胞急性淋巴细胞白血病
T淋巴母细胞白血病/淋巴瘤
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with relapsed or refractory T-lymphoblastic leukemia/Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-in-human dual-epitope nanobody anti-CD5 CAR-T for relapsed/refractory T-ALL/PTCL: Phase I dose-escalation and expansion results from the CONQUER trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: Real-world outcomes in ctDNA-detected FGFR2-positive advanced cholangiocarcinoma did not improve with the addition of immune checkpoint inhibitors to first-line GemCis. In contrast, first-line FGFR inhibition was associated with longer treatment duration and delayed need for subsequent therapy, supporting ctDNA testing to inform biomarker-driven first-line treatment selection and sequencing strategies.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with advanced cholangiocarcinoma and ctDNA-detected FGFR2 fusions detected prior to first-line therapy were analyzed, comparing targeted therapy with GemCis with or without immune checkpoint inhibitors.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-line GemCis ± immunotherapy vs FGFR inhibition in ctDNA-detected FGFR2 fusion–positive advanced cholangiocarcinoma: A real-world analysis.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this real-world cohort of patients with previously treated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma receiving FGFR inhibitors, median overall survival was 12 months and median time to next treatment was 17 months. Early toxicity was predominantly characterized by hyperphosphatemia, providing clinically relevant real-world context for outcomes and toxicity monitoring in routine practice.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Adults aged 18 years or older with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who initiated pemigatinib or futibatinib on or after 04/01/2020 and had evidence of prior systemic anticancer therapy were included.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Real-world outcomes and safety of FGFR inhibitors in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: A TriNetX analysis.

data.clinical_result_summary: Sequential intratumoral administration of OH2 and BS006 in heavily pre-treated patients is feasible and safe and results in reasonable disease control rate, with some patients achieving long-term clinical benefits. The study supports the clinical relevance of an HSV2-based platform combination of two oncolytic viruses encoding GM-CSF and T-cell redirected bispecific antibodies to warm up the cold tumor microenvironment, and further clinical research is warranted.
clinical_result_indication_detail: heavily pre-treated patients with advanced solid tumors
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Safety and preliminary efficacy of OH2 combined with BS006 sequential intratumoral injection in patients with advanced solid tumors: An open-label, dose-escalation phase Ib/II study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Longer TIS-3 intervals were associated with longer survival times in 3rd-line treatment. This observation was particularly evident for patients receiving cetuximab rechallenge, but was also observed in those receiving investigator’s choice.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with RAS-wildtype metastatic colorectal cancer receiving 3rd-line treatment who had responded to induction therapy and were re-evaluated for RAS status, with RAS mutations excluded before randomization.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: FIRE-4 (AIO KRK-0114): Efficacy of third-line rechallenge with cetuximab versus investigator’s choice in relation to the interval between initial and third-line anti-EGFR therapy.

data.clinical_result_summary: Donafenib as adjuvant therapy may be a potentially effective way to prevent HCC recurrence after curative surgery. The findings should be validated in a larger, prospectively evaluated sample.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with HCC following hepatectomy treated with donafenib in routine practice at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University were enrolled if they were 75 years or younger, had been diagnosed with HCC, showed no evidence of recurrence at radiological follow-up within one month after hepatectomy, had at least one high recurrence risk factor such as tumor diameter ≥5 cm, tumor number ≥2, microvascular invasion, or serum alpha-fetoprotein level before surgery ≥400 ng/mL, and had adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Postoperative adjuvant therapy of donafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma with high-risk recurrence factors: A real world, prospective, observational study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with biosimilar intravenous pertuzumab and trastuzumab achieved pathological response and surgical outcomes comparable to Phesgo in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer. These findings support biosimilar-based dual HER2 blockade as an effective and affordable neoadjuvant strategy, particularly for improving access to standard-of-care therapy in resource-constrained settings.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and dual HER2 blockade using either intravenous biosimilar pertuzumab with trastuzumab or the subcutaneous fixed-dose combination pertuzumab/trastuzumab/hyaluronidase, Phesgo.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Neoadjuvant intravenous biosimilar pertuzumab and trastuzumab versus subcutaneous pertuzumab/trastuzumab/hyaluronidase (Phesgo) in HER2-positive breast cancer: A real-world comparative study.

data.clinical_result_summary: AiBW dosing effectively reduced pharmacokinetic variability compared with TBW dosing, providing more consistent exposure across body weight. Higher ADC exposure was associated with increased efficacy, but also with a higher incidence of manageable treatment-related adverse events. AiBW optimizes the risk-benefit profile across body weight.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with advanced solid tumors, including patients with ovarian cancer.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Consideration of adjusted ideal body weight dosing in BG-C9074 (B7-H4–targeting ADC) from pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety perspectives.

data.clinical_result_summary: Cal-PEG had a safety profile consistent with asparaginase class toxicity and, as part of a multidrug chemotherapy regimen, provided sustained asparagine depletion in newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-negative acute lymphoblastic leukemia patients aged ≥22 years. In light of the observed high-grade treatment-related adverse events, future studies will evaluate different Cal-PEG doses for this patient population.
clinical_result_indication_detail: pts aged ≥22 years with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-negative acute lymphoblastic leukemia
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Preliminary results of an open-label, single-arm phase 2/3 trial (SPARK-ALL) of calaspargase pegol in adults with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome–negative acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

data.clinical_result_summary: Trilaciclib demonstrated effective myeloprotection and immunoregulation in gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, with primary prophylaxis showing a favorable trend. Grade ≥3 chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression rates were ≤5.88% in the adjuvant setting and ≤3.49% in the metastatic setting, with no new safety signals.
clinical_result_indication_detail: GAC/GEJAC patients, post-D2/R0 resection receiving adjuvant chemotherapy (Cohort 1)
GAC/GEJAC patients with metastatic patients receiving first-line combination chemotherapy (cohort 2)
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Trilaciclib for myeloprotection in adjuvant and first-line chemotherapy for advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: A multicohort study.

data.clinical_result_summary: The combination of both dose levels of PLD with PEM was well tolerated, active, and feasible for extended treatment with durable responses in heavily pretreated ER-positive metastatic breast cancer patients. The favorable response and survival data suggest that PEM has a significant contribution to the anti-tumor effect, and a randomized study based on this regimen is warranted.
clinical_result_indication_detail: estrogen receptor-positive, endocrine-resistant breast cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Nanochemo-immunotherapy of ER-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC) with PEG-liposomal doxorubicin (PLD) and pembrolizumab (PEM).

data.clinical_result_summary: The combination of pembrolizumab and cytotoxic chemotherapy did not substantially change antitumor control activity relative to historical controls in patients with advanced salivary or thyroid cancers. There were no statistically significant differences in PFS and OS between adenoid cystic and non-adenoid cystic subtypes.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with advanced thyroid cancers
patients with advanced salivary gland
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Anti–PD-1 immunotherapy with chemotherapy for poorly chemo-responsive thyroid and salivary gland tumors: The iPRIME study.

data.clinical_result_summary: The combination of liposomal irinotecan, cisplatin, and bevacizumab shows promising activity and manageable toxicity in recurrent high-grade glioma. This ongoing clinical trial may offer a new option for this difficult-to-treat population, with more data to be disclosed in the future.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with confirmed recurrent high-grade glioma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Phase II study of liposomal irinotecan in combination with cisplatin and bevacizumab for high-grade recurrent glioma.

data.clinical_result_summary: The trial was limited by early termination and did not statistically demonstrate the non-inferiority of pembrolizumab monotherapy for progression-free survival. Numerical overall survival favored pembrolizumab monotherapy despite a lower response rate, suggesting that pembrolizumab monotherapy remains a robust treatment option with a favorable safety profile for patients with PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, while adding chemotherapy may provide higher initial response rates.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A randomized phase III study of pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab with carboplatin plus pemetrexed for locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous non–small cell lung cancer with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%: LAPLACE-50.

data.clinical_result_summary: Among patients with MET exon 14 skipping mutation metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, first-line IO ± chemotherapy was associated with better overall survival than MET TKI. The survival advantage appeared especially pronounced in patients with PD-L1 ≥50, whereas MET TKI was associated with longer progression-free survival in patients with PD-L1 <50.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Metastatic non-small cell lung cancer patients with MET exon 14 skipping mutations who received first-line therapy with either MET TKI or immune checkpoint inhibitors ± chemotherapy, excluding patients with EGFR alterations.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Real-world effectiveness of MET inhibitors versus immunotherapy ± chemotherapy in 1L for patients with MET exon 14 skipping mutations in non-small cell lung cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: Donafenib plus hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy and PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies showed potentially superior anti-HCC efficacy compared with bevacizumab plus the same backbone treatment in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, with no significant difference in overall adverse event incidence.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients diagnosed with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma and initially treated with DonaHP or BevHP at the Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center between April 2022 and July 2023.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Efficacy and safety analysis of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies combined with donafenib or bevacizumab in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

data.clinical_result_summary: In resected EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer, adjuvant erlotinib did not improve overall survival but improved disease-free survival. Additional studies are exploring efficacy in selected subsets of patients using genomics and proteomic analyses.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with completely resected stage IB (≥4 cm), II, or IIIA non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations
clinical_result_layer_factor: stage, prior chemotherapy, EGFR mutation subtype, and ECOG performance status
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Adjuvant erlotinib versus observation after complete resection of EGFR-mutant NSCLC: Final overall survival results of Alliance A081105.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this exploratory trial, 'R-ISV-RO' with concurrent immunotherapy demonstrated promising efficacy for both primary and distant tumors, especially for sarcomas. Systemic immune response and metabolic remodeling were also observed after therapy.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Advanced solid tumors
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Enhanced local and systemic efficacy in refractory solid tumors via integrated intra-tumoral injection and radiotherapy: A study of the ‘R-ISV-RO’ modality.

data.clinical_result_summary: As frontline therapy, tagraxofusp with Hyper-CVAD and venetoclax showed promising safety, with no early mortality or high-grade capillary leak syndrome. The regimen produced high response rates, enabled frequent stem cell transplant consolidation, and was associated with no central nervous system relapse.
clinical_result_indication_name: 母细胞性浆细胞样树突细胞肿瘤
clinical_result_indication_detail: Adults with newly diagnosed blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.
Adults with relapsed/refractory blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A phase II trial of tagraxofusp, hyper-CVAD, and venetoclax for patients with newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory BPDCN.

data.clinical_result_summary: The combination of TACE/HAIC, bevacizumab, and tislelizumab demonstrated promising disease control and survival benefit with a manageable safety profile as third-line therapy for microsatellite stable colorectal cancer with unresectable liver metastases. Baseline BMI and extrahepatic metastatic burden may help identify patients more likely to benefit, and further studies are warranted to optimize the regimen and validate predictive biomarkers.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study enrolled patients with microsatellite stable colorectal cancer and unresectable liver metastases who had failed at least two prior systemic therapies, in the third-line treatment setting.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: TACE/HAIC combined with bevacizumab and tislelizumab as third-line therapy for colorectal cancer with unresectable liver metastases: A prospective, observational real-world study (TABTiC).

data.clinical_result_summary: This first-in-human study targeting CDH17 in patients with gastrointestinal cancer showed a tolerable safety profile for cabotamig up to 0.32 mg/kg. Step-up dosing appeared to mitigate dose-responsive on-target tumor cytokine release syndrome, with minimal on-target normal gastrointestinal mucosal effects, and dose-responsive biomarker anti-tumor activity was observed.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Pts ≥18 years with locally advanced or metastatic CDH17+ GI cancers refractory to therapies
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Phase 1, FIH study of cabotamig, a TCE CDH17 X CD3, in CDH17-expressing GI malignancies.

data.clinical_result_summary: Durvalumab combined with chemoradiation therapy demonstrated promising 1-year disease-free survival and survival outcomes compared with previously reported chemoradiation therapy outcomes, with a manageable safety profile. CRT-D was considered a safe treatment with side effects consistent with known effects of chemoradiation therapy and durvalumab, and further investigation is warranted.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients had T2–T4aN0–N2M0 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Feasibility and safety results from RAD-IO: A multi-stage trial of durvalumab with chemoradiotherapy with 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin C in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: SYS6043 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and robust, cross-tumor antitumor activity in a large population of patients with advanced solid tumors. The magnitude and consistency of responses across multiple histologies, including treatment-refractory tumors such as small cell lung cancer, support SYS6043 as a promising therapeutic candidate warranting further clinical and translational investigation.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - OC
patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - CC
patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - BC
patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - EC
patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - nsq-NSCLC
patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - SCLC
patients (18–75 years) had advanced solid tumors refractory to or progressing after standard therapies - NPC
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-in-human study of SYS6043, a novel B7-H3–targeting antibody-drug conjugate, in patients with advanced pan-tumor malignancies.

data.clinical_result_summary: Using clinical practice data, relugolix treatment led to successful testosterone suppression, low rates of documented serious adverse events and cardiovascular-related serious adverse events, and high adherence at 6 months in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. Results were similar in patients initiating relugolix monotherapy and combination therapy.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study enrolled patients with prostate cancer who had initiated relugolix within 1 month before study enrollment and intended to remain on relugolix for at least 4 months; this subgroup analysis assessed patients with metastatic prostate cancer initiating relugolix monotherapy or relugolix in combination with other systemic prostate therapies.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Testosterone suppression, safety, and adherence with relugolix in patients with metastatic prostate cancer: 6-month subgroup analysis of the OPTYX study.

data.clinical_result_summary: In Part 1B of OLYMPIA-3, the safety profile of odronextamab-CHOP was generally manageable and preliminary efficacy was encouraging, with no meaningful differences between regimens. The less frequent odronextamab dosing regimen with CHOP was selected as the recommended Phase 3 dose for Part 2.
clinical_result_indication_detail: pts aged ≥18 years with untreated CD20+ DLBCL (PART 1B)
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-line odronextamab (Odro) plus chemotherapy (CHOP) in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL): OLYMPIA-3 Part 1B results.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this phase 2 trial, adding olaparib to radium-223 achieved superior radiographic progression-free survival without significant detriment to patient-reported quality of life or pain compared with radium-223 alone. These findings support the tolerability of the combination in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Quality of life analysis from a multicenter, randomized, phase 2, investigator-initiated ETCTN trial of olaparib + radium-223 versus radium-223 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases (COMRADE).

data.clinical_result_summary: Neoadjuvant firmonertinib combined with chemotherapy showed a promising surgical conversion rate and a manageable safety profile in resectable stage II-IIIB EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. The findings support its feasibility for further study.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with stage II-IIIB EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Firmonertinib combined with cisplatin/carboplatin plus pemetrexed as neoadjuvant therapy in resectable stage II-IIIb EGFR-mutated non–small cell lung cancer: A single-arm, single-center, open-label phase II study.

data.clinical_result_summary: The combination of tislelizumab with chemoradiotherapy demonstrated promising efficacy and acceptable safety in patients with advanced biliary tract cancer. CD103+CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells were identified as a potential predictive biomarker.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with advanced biliary tract cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-line tislelizumab plus chemoradiotherapy for patients with advanced biliary tract cancer: A prospective, biomolecular exploratory, phase II trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this blinded, pooled safety analysis of a randomized phase 2 trial in newly diagnosed glioblastoma, the study treatment was well tolerated and no new safety signals were identified. Treatment allocation remains blinded, and efficacy outcomes and arm-specific safety analyses will be reported after completion of the primary endpoint analysis.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A phase 2 double-blind, randomized, prospective, placebo-controlled study of NanO₂ combined with radiation and temozolomide in patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma: RESTORE.

data.clinical_result_summary: [225Ac]Ac-PSMA-XT showed a favorable and manageable safety profile with no dose-limiting toxicities observed up to 100 kBq/kg. Early efficacy signals were highly encouraging, with deep PSA declines and durable disease control in this heavily pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer population. These data support continued dose escalation and further development of this alpha-emitting PSMA-targeted therapy.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A phase I study of [225Ac]Ac-PSMA-XT, a novel alpha-particle–emitting radioligand therapy, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: Prior ESA therapy did not appear to increase thrombotic risk after luspatercept initiation in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes. The findings support the thrombotic safety profile of luspatercept in prior ESA-exposed patients, but prospective validation is warranted.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Adults with myelodysplastic syndromes treated with luspatercept and no prior venous or arterial thromboembolism were stratified into prior ESA-exposed versus ESA-naive cohorts.
clinical_result_layer_factor: demographics, comorbidities/risk factors, anticoagulation/antiplatelet use, and baseline hematologic parameters
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Impact of prior exposure to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESA) on thromboembolic events in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes receiving luspatercept: A real-world TriNetX-based study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Patients with recurrent resectable osteosarcoma limited to the lung parenchyma can be included as a separate cohort in phase II trials of novel agents. In this cohort, pre-surgical treatment with olaparib and ceralasertib followed by surgical resection of pulmonary nodules and collection of paired tumor samples was feasible. The 12-month EFS was 40%, but the confidence interval was wide and crossed the historical 12-month EFS confidence interval of 20% from prior COG studies.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with recurrent osteosarcoma and measurable unresectable disease (cohort 2, Lung-only resectable)
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Phase II trial of olaparib and ceralasertib in patients with recurrent osteosarcoma: Lung-only resectable cohort efficacy and correlative biomarker results.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this phase 2 trial, adding olaparib to radium-223 achieved superior radiographic progression-free survival without significant detriment to patient-reported quality of life or pain compared with radium-223 alone. These findings support the tolerability of the combination in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Quality of life analysis from a multicenter, randomized, phase 2, investigator-initiated ETCTN trial of olaparib + radium-223 versus radium-223 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases (COMRADE).

data.clinical_result_summary: In this large real-world cohort of patients with chronic myeloid leukemia who discontinued imatinib, survival outcomes after second-line TKI therapy were similar among dasatinib, bosutinib, and nilotinib, while asciminib showed lower mortality. Higher mortality with ponatinib may reflect differences in underlying mutation profiles or drug side effects. These findings support individualized selection of second-line TKIs after imatinib discontinuation.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included adult patients older than 18 years with BCR-ABL positive chronic myeloid leukemia who received imatinib and subsequently started a second-line tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Beyond imatinib: Real-world mortality patterns across modern second-line TKIs in CML.

data.clinical_result_summary: With 5 years of follow-up, first-line nivolumab plus relatlimab continued to demonstrate durable, clinically meaningful long-term improvements in PFS, OS, ORR, and MSS versus nivolumab in advanced melanoma. Safety remained consistent with prior reports, with no new or unexpected safety signals.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with Previously Untreated Metastatic or Unresectable Melanoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Nivolumab + relatlimab (NIVO + RELA) in advanced melanoma: 5-year update of RELATIVITY-047.

data.clinical_result_summary: Single-dose administration of 225Ac-MTI-201 with dose escalation to 76 μCi appears safe and feasible in metastatic uveal melanoma. Disease stability in this difficult-to-treat population is encouraging, and a multi-dose study of 225Ac-MTI-201 in metastatic uveal melanoma is planned pending final patient DLT assessment.
clinical_result_indication_detail: mUM patients (pts) with progressive disease after at least 1 prior systemic or liver-directed therapy
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Final results of a first-in-human study of the MC1R-targeting radiopharmaceutical 225actinium MTI-201 (225Ac-MTI-201) in metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM).

data.clinical_result_summary: The combination of TACE/HAIC, bevacizumab, and tislelizumab demonstrated promising disease control and survival benefit with a manageable safety profile as third-line therapy for microsatellite stable colorectal cancer with unresectable liver metastases. Baseline BMI and extrahepatic metastatic burden may help identify patients more likely to benefit, and further studies are warranted to optimize the regimen and validate predictive biomarkers.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study enrolled patients with microsatellite stable colorectal cancer and unresectable liver metastases who had failed at least two prior systemic therapies, in the third-line treatment setting.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: TACE/HAIC combined with bevacizumab and tislelizumab as third-line therapy for colorectal cancer with unresectable liver metastases: A prospective, observational real-world study (TABTiC).

data.clinical_result_summary: In patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma who received atezolizumab plus bevacizumab or durvalumab plus tremelimumab as first-line systemic therapy, safety profiles differed between cohorts, while no significant difference in median overall survival was observed. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab was associated with higher risk of hypertension and proteinuria, whereas durvalumab plus tremelimumab was associated with higher risk of immune-mediated colitis and hospitalization.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included adult patients with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma, specifically patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma who received atezolizumab plus bevacizumab or durvalumab plus tremelimumab as first-line systemic therapy.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Comparative outcomes of first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (A+B) and durvalumab plus tremelimumab (D+T) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

data.clinical_result_summary: Baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT-derived SUVmax is a strong prognostic biomarker in patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer treated with first-line pembrolizumab and chemotherapy. High SUVmax identifies a subgroup of patients with substantially poorer PFS and OS and may help guide risk-adapted therapeutic strategies.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Female patients in Poland, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia with histologically confirmed metastatic triple-negative breast cancer who received first-line pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy outside of clinical trials and underwent baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT were included.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Prognostic value of baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT in first-line pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: UGN-102 maintained stable quality-of-life scores across NMIBC24 domains and was generally preferred by patients over surgical resections. These insights support shared decision making by enabling clinicians to discuss trade-offs between procedural convenience and treatment invasiveness in recurrent low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer management.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with biopsy-confirmed low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer and at least 1 previous non-muscle invasive bladder cancer episode at baseline, with semi-structured prospective phone interviews conducted in 32 US-based patients.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Patient experiences with UGN-102 for recurrent low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC): Insights for shared decision making.

data.clinical_result_summary: Inotuzumab ozogamicin exposure before CAR-T therapy was associated with higher rates of CRS/ICANS, hepatic toxicity, and increased mortality in adults with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The authors suggested that prior inotuzumab use may identify a subgroup predisposed to more complications who could benefit from additional supportive measures and monitoring after CAR-T.
clinical_result_indication_name: B细胞急性淋巴细胞白血病
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included adults >18 years of age with relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia who subsequently received CAR-T therapy, analyzed according to prior inotuzumab exposure.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Outcomes following CAR-T therapy in adults with relapsed/refractory B-ALL according to prior inotuzumab exposure.

data.clinical_result_summary: Velzatinib demonstrated broad activity against clinically relevant KIT mutations in patients with advanced and/or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumors and substantially reduced circulating tumor DNA levels across a broad spectrum of KIT mutation profiles. Baseline exon-level KIT mutation status and circulating tumor DNA detectability may provide useful prognostic and predictive information, supporting further study of the relationship between clinical benefit and molecular response.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with metastatic and/or surgically unresectable GIST after failure of imatinib and other approved drugs
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Efficacy of velzatinib (IDRX-42) in patients with advanced/metastatic GIST by line of therapy and circulating tumor DNA response in the phase 1/1b StrateGIST 1 trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: Adding galunisertib to enzalutamide did not improve radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival, or PSA response compared with enzalutamide alone in chemotherapy-naive patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing on abiraterone. These findings do not support further development of galunisertib plus enzalutamide in this setting.
clinical_result_indication_detail: chemotherapy-naive patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
clinical_result_primary_endpoint_cn: 中位影像学无进展生存期
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Can TGF-β inhibition (galunisertib) enhance response to enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)?: Results from a randomized phase II trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: In patients with metastatic EGFR gene amplification esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, nimotuzumab plus TP as first-line treatment significantly improved overall survival and progression-free survival. The regimen had a good safety profile.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with metastatic EGFR gene amplification esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Nimotuzumab combined with paclitaxel and cisplatin as first-line treatment for metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: A prospective, multicenter, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical study.

data.clinical_result_summary: GC101 TIL significantly improved PFS and ORR versus investigator-choice chemotherapy in anti-PD-1-resistant melanoma. The safety profile was manageable, supporting its potential as a new later-line therapy.
clinical_result_indication_detail: advanced melanoma patients resistant to PD-1 antibodies
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A multicenter, randomized, controlled, open-label, phase II trial of autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (GC101 TIL) in patients with advanced melanoma.

data.clinical_result_summary: Intraperitoneal intratumoral LPS delivery in peritoneal metastases was safe and biologically active. It induced reproducible innate-dominant immune and metabolic remodeling, supporting regional TLR4 agonism as a feasible strategy for peritoneal malignancies.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with peritoneal metastases from gastrointestinal malignancies undergoing diagnostic laparoscopy
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A phase I window-of-opportunity trial of intraperitoneal, intratumoral lipopolysaccharide in peritoneal metastases: Safety and immune remodeling from the RIOT-1 study.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this large real-world cohort of ICI-treated patients with pre-existing autoimmune disease, baseline prednisone use was not associated with a statistically significant increase in mortality, despite higher rates of hospitalization and sepsis. These findings may suggest that selected patients with autoimmune disease receiving baseline corticosteroids may still derive survival benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included adult patients with documented pre-existing autoimmune disease who received immune checkpoint inhibitors.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in patients with pre-existing autoimmune disease: A propensity-matched real-world analysis of baseline corticosteroid use.

Grade ≥3 chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression rates were ≤5.88% in the adjuvant setting and ≤3.49% in the metastatic setting, with no new safety signals.
clinical_result_indication_detail: GAC/GEJAC patients, post-D2/R0 resection receiving adjuvant chemotherapy (Cohort 1)
GAC/GEJAC patients with metastatic patients receiving first-line combination chemotherapy (cohort 2)
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Trilaciclib for myeloprotection in adjuvant and first-line chemotherapy for advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: A multicohort study.

data.clinical_result_summary: ABBV-706 monotherapy showed promising overall survival benefit in a heavily pretreated population with relapsed/refractory small cell lung cancer. The combination with budigalimab was feasible, with no new safety signals identified.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) SCLC
data.clinical_result_paper_title: ABBV-706 as monotherapy and in combination with budigalimab in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) small cell lung cancer (SCLC).

data.clinical_result_summary: For patients with locally advanced gastric cancer, intensifying perioperative chemotherapy with preoperative radiotherapy improved survival. This strategy was effective for high-risk cases requiring enhanced locoregional control.
clinical_result_indication_detail: stage cT3N2/N3M0, cT4aN+M0, or cT4bNanyM0 gastric or esophagogastric junction (EGJ, Siewert type II/III) adenocarcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by D2 gastrectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced gastric cancer (Neo-CRAG): A randomized, multicenter, phase 3 trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: Addition of gabapentin to tramadol during concurrent chemoradiation significantly reduced the need for opioid escalation for mucositis-related pain in patients with head and neck cancer. Although early pain scores were similar, gabapentin showed a clinically meaningful opioid-sparing effect and may be an effective strategy for managing concurrent chemoradiation-induced mucositis pain.

clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with HNSCC receiving radical or adjuvant CTRT who developed CTCAE v5.0 grade ≥1 mucositis with pain

data.clinical_result_summary: SL105, an autologous dual-epitope nanobody CD5 CAR-T therapy, demonstrated a favorable safety profile and encouraging efficacy in patients with relapsed or refractory T-ALL/PTCL. The recommended phase 2 dose was established, supporting further evaluation in an ongoing phase 2 study.
clinical_result_indication_name: T细胞急性淋巴细胞白血病
T淋巴母细胞白血病/淋巴瘤
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with relapsed or refractory T-lymphoblastic leukemia/Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-in-human dual-epitope nanobody anti-CD5 CAR-T for relapsed/refractory T-ALL/PTCL: Phase I dose-escalation and expansion results from the CONQUER trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: bTAE-HAIC combined with lenvatinib plus camrelizumab appears to be a promising first-line treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma with a high tumor burden. The regimen produced an exceptional objective response rate and encouraging survival outcomes with manageable toxicity.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with high tumor burden hepatocellular carcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A phase II study of bTAE-HAIC combined with lenvatinib and camrelizumab for patients with high tumor burden hepatocellular carcinoma: The TALEM-H trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: Synchronous and metachronous metastatic urothelial cancer treated with enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab have significantly different disease courses. Metachronous metastatic urothelial cancer has earlier progression on enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab, suggesting a need for more treatment options in refractory disease. Consolidation treatment for synchronous metastatic urothelial cancer requires further prospective trials to optimize outcomes.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included all consecutive patients with metastatic urothelial cancer treated with enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab at UTSW, grouped by synchronous metastatic urothelial cancer or metachronous metastatic urothelial cancer.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Clinical outcomes for patients (pts) with synchronous versus metachronous metastatic urothelial cancer (mUC) treated with enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (EV-P).

data.clinical_result_summary: CRD3874-SI demonstrated clinical activity with manageable safety in patients with advanced solid tumors. Dose level 0.9 mg/kg was described as biologically and clinically active, and a dose expansion phase at this dose level is planned in more than 5 histology-specific cohorts.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with advanced solid tumors
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Systemic third generation allosteric STING agonist CRD3874-SI, a novel immunotherapy, in patients with advanced solid tumors: Results from a single-agent phase I study.

data.clinical_result_summary: The SAKK 96/12 REDUSE trial demonstrated that denosumab every 12 weeks after a 3-month loading phase was non-inferior to every 4 weeks in patients with bone-metastatic breast cancer or castration-resistant prostate cancer. The every-12-weeks schedule showed lower rates of osteonecrosis of the jaw and hypocalcemia, suggesting a more favorable safety profile while maintaining comparable efficacy.
clinical_result_indication_detail: pts with metastatic breast cancer (BC) or castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and at least three bone metastases
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Prevalence of symptomatic skeletal events (SSE) with reduced denosumab (Dmab) dose density (every 12 weeks versus every 4 weeks): A randomized phase III non-inferiority trial SAKK 96/12 REDUSE.

data.clinical_result_summary: Volrustomig monotherapy showed an acceptable safety profile and encouraging activity in patients with recurrent/metastatic HNSCC. These findings support further clinical development of volrustomig in this setting.
clinical_result_indication_name_en: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (SCCHN)
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with recurrent/metastatic HNSCC
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Volrustomig monotherapy for recurrent/metastatic HNSCC: Substudy 2 of the eVOLVE-02 phase 2 study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Autologous NK cell infusion as consolidation therapy after first-line chemoradiotherapy for limited-stage SCLC showed promising preliminary progression-free and overall survival benefits, with good tolerability and safety.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Autologous natural killer cell infusion as consolidation therapy after first-line chemoradiotherapy for limited-stage small-cell lung cancer: A randomized, controlled, open-label, single-center phase II clinical study.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this real-world cohort, mFOLFIRINOX and PAXG showed comparable efficacy as first-line regimens in patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer and metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Larger matched cohorts are needed for validation.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included consecutive patients with unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma treated with FOLFIRINOX or modified FOLFIRINOX, or PAXG, as first-line therapy between 2020 and 2024 at the Veneto Institute of Oncology in Padua, Italy.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: PAXG versus (m)FOLFIRINOX as first-Line therapy for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer: A real-world, propensity-weighted analysis.

data.clinical_result_summary: Neoadjuvant tislelizumab monotherapy showed favorable efficacy and a manageable safety profile in locally advanced deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high colon cancer, with high pathological complete response rates and feasible non-operative management for clinical complete response patients. Minimal residual disease monitoring provided valuable real-time assessment of treatment response to guide surgical and surveillance decisions, although longer follow-up is needed to confirm response durability, particularly in non-operative management patients.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with locally advanced deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high colon adenocarcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Efficacy and safety of tislelizumab as neoadjuvant therapy combined with MRD monitoring in locally advanced dMMR/MSI-H colon cancer: A prospective pilot study.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this real-world cohort of multiple myeloma patients treated with bispecific antibodies, early immunoglobulin replacement was associated with lower risks of serious infection and early mortality. These findings suggest a potential role for immunoglobulin replacement in reducing early infectious risk among patients receiving bispecific antibodies and support further prospective evaluation.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Adults aged ≥18 years with multiple myeloma who initiated bispecific antibody therapy with teclistamab, elranatamab, or talquetamab were included.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Association of immunoglobulin replacement with infection and mortality outcomes in multiple myeloma patients receiving bispecific antibodies: A TriNetX analysis.

data.clinical_result_summary: For patients with locally advanced gastric cancer, intensifying perioperative chemotherapy with preoperative radiotherapy improved survival. This strategy was effective for high-risk cases requiring enhanced locoregional control.
clinical_result_indication_detail: stage cT3N2/N3M0, cT4aN+M0, or cT4bNanyM0 gastric or esophagogastric junction (EGJ, Siewert type II/III) adenocarcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by D2 gastrectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced gastric cancer (Neo-CRAG): A randomized, multicenter, phase 3 trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory/resistant cutaneous melanoma population enriched with primary immune checkpoint inhibitor-resistant patients, botensilimab plus balstilimab showed durable responses, encouraging survival, and a stronger signal in patients who had prior conventional anti-CTLA-4. Botensilimab monotherapy also showed activity, supporting a differentiated mechanism for botensilimab and continued development of botensilimab plus balstilimab, including for patients with dual immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory/resistant cutaneous melanoma.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with advanced cutaneous melanoma refractory/resistant to prior anti-PD-(L)1 ± CTLA-4
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Botensilimab (BOT) ± balstilimab (BAL) in patients (pts) with advanced cutaneous melanoma (cMEL) refractory/resistant (R/R) to anti–PD-(L)1 ± CTLA-4: A phase 2 trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: HB-200 therapy can clear TTMV-HPV DNA detected by NavDx in a subset of patients with HPV16+ head and neck squamous cell carcinoma minimal residual disease and induces E6/E7 antigen-specific T-cells. Treatment of minimal residual disease is feasible, and further study is warranted to establish the therapeutic standard.
clinical_result_indication_name_en: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (SCCHN)
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with HPV16+ head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and detectable TTMV-HPVDNA after definitive therapy
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Pilot study of HB-200 in patients with HPV16+ head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and detectable TTMV-HPVDNA after definitive therapy.

data.clinical_result_summary: Addition of gabapentin to tramadol during concurrent chemoradiation significantly reduced the need for opioid escalation for mucositis-related pain in patients with head and neck cancer. Although early pain scores were similar, gabapentin showed a clinically meaningful opioid-sparing effect and may be an effective strategy for managing concurrent chemoradiation-induced mucositis pain.
clinical_result_indication_name: 放化疗引起的口腔溃疡
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with HNSCC receiving radical or adjuvant CTRT who developed CTCAE v5.0 grade ≥1 mucositis with pain
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Gabapentin plus tramadol versus tramadol alone for chemoradiotherapy-induced oral mucositis pain in head and neck cancer: Results of a randomized phase III trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: Reirradiation with NBTXR3 with SBRT and anti-PD-1 therapy was feasible in recurrent or recurrent plus metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, with an adverse effect profile expected for this clinical setting. Encouraging preliminary efficacy outcomes were observed, warranting further investigation.
clinical_result_indication_name_en: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (SCCHN)
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with recurrent or metastatic head & neck squamous cell carcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Reirradiation with NBTXR3/SBRT in combination with nivolumab or pembrolizumab for the treatment of patients with recurrent or metastatic head & neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) in the phase I trial study 1100.

data.clinical_result_summary: Donafenib as adjuvant therapy may be a potentially effective way to prevent HCC recurrence after curative surgery. The findings should be validated in a larger, prospectively evaluated sample.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with HCC following hepatectomy treated with donafenib in routine practice at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University were enrolled if they were 75 years or younger, had been diagnosed with HCC, showed no evidence of recurrence at radiological follow-up within one month after hepatectomy, had at least one high recurrence risk factor such as tumor diameter ≥5 cm, tumor number ≥2, microvascular invasion, or serum alpha-fetoprotein level before surgery ≥400 ng/mL, and had adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Postoperative adjuvant therapy of donafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma with high-risk recurrence factors: A real world, prospective, observational study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Irinotecan liposome at a dose of 50 mg/m2 in the NALIRIFOX regimen showed manageable safety and promising efficacy as first-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with histologically confirmed and initially unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer
data.clinical_result_paper_title: NALIRIFOX plus targeted therapy as first-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer: A phase I study.

data.clinical_result_summary: BFv plus toripalimab in patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma demonstrated remarkable efficacy and a well-tolerated safety profile. A pivotal phase 3 study is ongoing.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Bulumtatug fuvedotin (BFv; 9MW2821) plus toripalimab in patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC): Follow-up results from a phase 1b/2 study.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this phase 2 trial, adding olaparib to radium-223 achieved superior radiographic progression-free survival without significant detriment to patient-reported quality of life or pain compared with radium-223 alone. These findings support the tolerability of the combination in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Quality of life analysis from a multicenter, randomized, phase 2, investigator-initiated ETCTN trial of olaparib + radium-223 versus radium-223 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases (COMRADE).

data.clinical_result_summary: Autologous TIL monotherapy was feasible and safe in Asian patients with diverse solid tumors. The study showed effective TIL therapy and potent anti-tumor activity of genetically enhanced ASS1 KO and CEP20 KO TILs, providing mechanistic insights that may guide optimization of TIL therapy for broader clinical application.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Asian patients with advanced melanoma, cervical, lung, or head and neck cancers.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (LM103 infusion) in solid tumors: A phase I trial evaluating clinical and immunological anti-tumor activity.

data.clinical_result_summary: Autologous TIL monotherapy was feasible and safe in Asian patients with diverse solid tumors. The study showed effective TIL therapy and potent anti-tumor activity of genetically enhanced ASS1 KO and CEP20 KO TILs, providing mechanistic insights that may guide optimization of TIL therapy for broader clinical application.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Asian patients with advanced melanoma, cervical, lung, or head and neck cancers.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (LM103 infusion) in solid tumors: A phase I trial evaluating clinical and immunological anti-tumor activity.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this limited case series of patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2/neu-positive metastatic breast cancer, fulvestrant, abemaciclib, and trastuzumab were associated with systemic control after multiple prior lines of treatment. Prolonged CNS benefit was reported in two patients with CNS metastases, including stabilization for 20 months in one patient and 31 months of CNS free progression in another.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The case series included six patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2/neu-positive metastatic breast cancer, including two patients with CNS involvement.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Late line treatment in hormone receptor positive, her 2 neu positive metastatic breast cancer with fulvestrant, abemaciclib, and trastuzumab, including prolonged CNS control.

data.clinical_result_summary: Results from inMMyCAR continue to demonstrate compelling early clinical activity of KLN-1010 in patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. All patients achieved early MRD-negative responses with deepening IMWG responses over time, and activity was observed in extramedullary disease. KLN-1010 was generally well tolerated, with manageable infusion-related reactions and cytokine release syndrome, and no ICANS or delayed neurotoxicity.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Updated results from inMMyCAR, the ongoing first-in-human phase 1 study of KLN-1010 in patients (pts) with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM).

data.clinical_result_summary: RP2 with or without nivolumab was well tolerated in patients with both superficial and deep visceral metastases. Durable responses were observed with RP2 monotherapy and RP2 plus nivolumab in heavily pretreated patients with diverse tumors, with evidence of systemic anti-tumor immune activity including tumor reduction in distant non-injected lesions.
clinical_result_indication_detail: pts had advanced/metastatic solid tumors with ≥1 measurable, injectable lesion (≥1 cm) and had progressed following, or could not tolerate, available standard therapy
data.clinical_result_paper_title: RP2 oncolytic immunotherapy alone and in combination with nivolumab (nivo) in patients with advanced solid tumors: Final safety, efficacy, and biomarker results from the phase 1 first-in-human (FIH) study.

data.clinical_result_summary: SYS6043 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and robust, cross-tumor antitumor activity in a large population of patients with advanced solid tumors. The magnitude and consistency of responses across multiple histologies, including treatment-refractory tumors such as small cell lung cancer, support SYS6043 as a promising therapeutic candidate warranting further clinical and translational investigation.

data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-in-human study of SYS6043, a novel B7-H3–targeting antibody-drug conjugate, in patients with advanced pan-tumor malignancies.

data.clinical_result_summary: In a propensity-matched real-world cohort of patients with gastric cancer, durvalumab was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality and MACE at 1-year, 3-year, and lifetime follow-up compared with pembrolizumab. Although limited by the observational design and potential residual confounding, these findings suggest a favorable survival and cardiovascular risk profile for durvalumab in this population and support prospective randomized studies to confirm the results.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with gastric cancer treated with pembrolizumab or durvalumab.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Cardiovascular outcomes of durvalumab versus pembrolizumab in gastric cancer: A propensity‑matched TriNetX analysis.

clinical_result_indication_detail: pts with metastatic breast cancer (BC) or castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and at least three bone metastases

data.clinical_result_summary: In a group of eight patients with advanced low grade serous ovarian carcinoma, everolimus and an aromatase inhibitor demonstrated a disease control rate of 87.5%, a median progression-free survival of 16.8 months, and a median overall survival of 26 months. Larger retrospective or prospective studies are needed, but this regimen should be considered for advanced, recurrent low grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with advanced and recurrent low grade serous ovarian carcinoma from a single tertiary-care institution were treated with everolimus and an aromatase inhibitor between 2000 and 2025; six had stage IIIC disease, two had stage IVB disease, and patients had received 1-6 prior lines of therapy before treatment.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Everolimus and aromatase inhibitors for advanced and recurrent low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.

data.clinical_result_summary: Trilaciclib demonstrated effective myeloprotection and immunoregulation in gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, with primary prophylaxis showing a favorable trend. Grade ≥3 chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression rates were ≤5.88% in the adjuvant setting and ≤3.49% in the metastatic setting, with no new safety signals.
clinical_result_indication_detail: GAC/GEJAC patients, post-D2/R0 resection receiving adjuvant chemotherapy (Cohort 1)
GAC/GEJAC patients with metastatic patients receiving first-line combination chemotherapy (cohort 2)
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Trilaciclib for myeloprotection in adjuvant and first-line chemotherapy for advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: A multicohort study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Updated results from the ASTRUM-004R study show that first-line serplulimab plus platinum-based therapy provides a significant survival benefit with a manageable safety profile in locally advanced or metastatic squamous non-small cell lung cancer. The findings are consistent with ASTRUM-004, and the long-term survival benefit warrants further validation with extended follow-up.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic squamous non-small cell lung cancer received first-line serplulimab plus platinum-based therapy.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: First-line serplulimab for locally advanced or metastatic squamous non–small cell lung cancer: Updated survival from the ASTRUM-004R trial.

data.clinical_result_summary: SYS6002 demonstrated a distinct safety profile from other Nectin-4 ADCs. Its promising efficacy in advanced urothelial carcinoma patients, including those progressing on prior MMAE-based ADCs, supports further phase 3 trials.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with advanced solid tumors who have failed or were intolerant to standard treatment
≥18 years with histologically confirmed Nectin-4 positive solid tumors who had failed or were intolerant to standard of care options

data.clinical_result_summary: SCRT plus consolidation chemotherapy was superior to LCRT plus consolidation chemotherapy in inducing complete or near complete clinical response in patients with rectal cancer. It emerged as the preferred regimen for further evaluation of an intentional watch-and-wait approach in a phase III study.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study enrolled patients in Chennai and Vellore, India, with rectal adenocarcinoma within 8 cm of the anal verge, T3N0 or T1-3N+ on magnetic resonance imaging, who required neoadjuvant radiation and surgery.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: SOCCER: A randomized phase II trial comparing complete clinical response after short course radiation or chemoradiation and consolidation chemotherapy in rectal cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this real-world study of first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer, surufatinib combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine-platinum chemotherapy showed encouraging preliminary efficacy and manageable safety. Larger sample size and longer follow-up are needed to validate these findings.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with biliary tract cancers and at least one measurable lesion per RECIST 1.1 criteria.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Efficacy and safety of surufatinib combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors plus chemotherapy in patients with biliary tract cancers: A real-world study.

data.clinical_result_summary: TCHP showed comparable efficacy to anthracycline-containing regimens with similar cardiac safety but higher hematological toxicity. Anthracycline-free regimens may be preferred for patients with cardiac risks, while advanced lymph node involvement remains a poor prognostic factor.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study analyzed HER2-positive breast cancer patients treated between 2015 and 2025 with neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy and surgery, focusing on HER2-positive early-stage breast cancer.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Comparison of anthracycline-containing and anthracycline-free neoadjuvant regimens in HER2-positive breast cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: Neoadjuvant and adjuvant enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab significantly improved event-free survival, overall survival, and pathological complete response rate compared with neoadjuvant gemcitabine plus cisplatin in participants with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were eligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy. The safety profile was consistent with prior experience with the combination, supporting enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab as an effective perioperative treatment option in this setting.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with MIBC who are cisplatin-eligible
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Neoadjuvant and adjuvant enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab for participants with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are eligible for cisplatin: Randomized, open-label, phase 3 KEYNOTE-B15 study.

data.clinical_result_summary: PHST001-101 is an open-label, first-in-human Phase 1 study evaluating PHST001 as monotherapy and in combination with chemotherapy in adults with advanced relapsed and/or refractory solid tumors. The study is currently enrolling patients in Phase 1a at Dose Level 8 (18 mg/kg), with no DLTs reported to date, and Phase 1b enrollment is anticipated to begin in early 2026.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Patients with solid tumors.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A phase 1 study of PHST001, an anti-CD24 monoclonal antibody, in adult patients with advanced relapsed and/or refractory solid tumors.

data.clinical_result_summary: Early on-treatment but not pre-treatment PPI exposure was strongly associated with inferior progression-free and overall survival in patients with advanced non-squamous NSCLC receiving the ABCP regimen. These findings support careful proton pump inhibitor use during the induction phase and should be validated in larger prospective cohorts.
clinical_result_indication_detail: Japanese patients with previously untreated advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Association of gut microbiota and peri-initiation proton pump inhibitor/antibiotic exposure with outcomes of atezolizumab-bevacizumab-carboplatin-paclitaxel regimen in patients with advanced non-squamous NSCLC: Prospective phase II study (K-TAIL-201).

data.clinical_result_summary: Treatment with STC-15 offers a new paradigm for the treatment of a broad range of sarcomas by halting the cell differentiation process from mesenchymal progenitors. Early biomarker data provide proof of mechanism in target engagement and changes in gene expression, consistent with pharmacological activity and clinical response. Further investigation of efficacy and biomarkers of STC-15 in a Phase 2 sarcoma study is ongoing.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with advanced malignancies
data.clinical_result_paper_title: A subset analysis of clinical activity and pharmacodynamic biomarkers in patients with sarcomas in the phase 1 dose-escalation study of STC-15, a METTL3 inhibitor.

data.clinical_result_summary: In this large real-world propensity-matched cohort of patients with malignant melanoma, nivolumab demonstrated a comparable overall safety profile to pembrolizumab, with lower risks of pneumonia and overall immune-related adverse events, but a higher risk of myocarditis. These findings provide clinically relevant real-world evidence to support individualized PD-1 inhibitor selection in melanoma.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included adult patients aged 18 years or older diagnosed with malignant melanoma who were treated with either nivolumab or pembrolizumab between January 2015 and December 2025, excluding patients receiving other immune checkpoint inhibitors.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Comparative real-world safety of nivolumab versus pembrolizumab in malignant melanoma: A propensity-matched cohort study.

data.clinical_result_summary: In patients with resected non-small cell lung cancer (≥4 cm or lymph node positive, EGFR/ALK negative), adjuvant nivolumab did not improve disease-free survival compared with observation, regardless of tumor PD-L1 expression. Treatment-related grade 3-5 toxicities were reported in 25% of patients.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients with resected NSCLC (≥4cm or LN+, EGFR/ALK-)
clinical_result_layer_factor: tumor histology, stage (AJCC 7th edition IB/IIA vs IIB/IIIA), prior adjuvant treatment, and PD-L1 status (<1% vs ≥1%)
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Randomized phase III study of nivolumab after surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy in NSCLC (ECOG-ACRIN EA5142, ALCHEMIST).

data.clinical_result_summary: Real-world first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab demonstrated meaningful clinical activity and manageable toxicity in metastatic urothelial carcinoma, with outcomes comparable to EV-302. Benefit appeared independent of prior platinum exposure, while patients not meeting EVITA eligibility derived minimal benefit, highlighting the importance of appropriate patient selection.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma, including metastatic urothelial carcinoma, treated with first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab at Alexandra Hospital since January 2024.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Real-world outcomes of first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab in metastatic urothelial carcinoma.

data.clinical_result_summary: Durvalumab combined with chemoradiation therapy demonstrated promising 1-year disease-free survival and survival outcomes compared with previously reported chemoradiation therapy outcomes, with a manageable safety profile. CRT-D was considered a safe treatment with side effects consistent with known effects of chemoradiation therapy and durvalumab, and further investigation is warranted.
clinical_result_indication_detail: patients had T2–T4aN0–N2M0 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Feasibility and safety results from RAD-IO: A multi-stage trial of durvalumab with chemoradiotherapy with 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin C in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

data.clinical_result_summary: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with biosimilar intravenous pertuzumab and trastuzumab achieved pathological response and surgical outcomes comparable to Phesgo in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer. These findings support biosimilar-based dual HER2 blockade as an effective and affordable neoadjuvant strategy, particularly for improving access to standard-of-care therapy in resource-constrained settings.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and dual HER2 blockade using either intravenous biosimilar pertuzumab with trastuzumab or the subcutaneous fixed-dose combination pertuzumab/trastuzumab/hyaluronidase, Phesgo.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Neoadjuvant intravenous biosimilar pertuzumab and trastuzumab versus subcutaneous pertuzumab/trastuzumab/hyaluronidase (Phesgo) in HER2-positive breast cancer: A real-world comparative study.

data.clinical_result_summary: Melphalan-based therapy with stem cell rescue yielded hematopoietic recovery, toxicity, and outcomes comparable to bispecific antibody bridging in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients awaiting CAR-T. The findings contrast with prior studies showing impaired recovery after intensive cytotoxic bridging, likely because stem cell rescue improves hematopoietic reserve. Prospective studies are warranted.
clinical_result_indication_detail: The study included relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients awaiting CAR-T who were bridged with melphalan-based therapy with stem cell rescue or talquetamab prior to CAR-T after apheresis.
data.clinical_result_paper_title: Efficacy and hematopoietic recovery of high-dose melphalan with stem cell rescue as bridging to CAR-T compared with non-intensive bridging in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.

data.clinical_result_summary: SYS6043 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and robust, cross-tumor antitumor activity in a large population of patients with advanced solid tumors. The magnitude and consistency of responses across multiple histologies, including treatment-refractory tumors such as small cell lung cancer, support SYS6043 as a promising therapeutic candidate warranting further clinical and translational investigation.
